note: Curated neighbourhoods, guides and local places. Edited by hand; merged into the site inventory at build time by scripts/discovery/export.ts.

entities.title: Inglewood
entities.summary: Calgary’s oldest historic neighbourhood, packed with red-brick heritage, artisan shops, craft breweries, and river pathways.
entities.description: Established in 1875 alongside Fort Calgary, Inglewood is Calgary’s cultural and heritage cornerstone. 9th Avenue SE features independent record stores, boutique coffee roasters, vintage clothing emporiums, and renowned dining, all framed by the curve of the Bow River and the Inglewood Bird Sanctuary.

sources.name: City of Calgary Heritage & Inglewood BRZ

image.alt: Inglewood historic brick streetscape and Bow River bend

entities.title: Kensington
entities.summary: An energetic, tree-lined urban village across the river from downtown, centred on 10th Street NW and Kensington Road.
entities.description: Kensington is Calgary’s iconic pedestrian-friendly urban hub. Home to over 250 independent businesses, vibrant patios, indie cinema, and Riley Park, it acts as the primary northwest gateway across the Bow River via the Peace Bridge.

image.alt: Kensington 10th Street NW and Peace Bridge entrance

entities.title: Beltline
entities.summary: Calgary’s vibrant inner-city core, buzzing with high-density dining, 17th Ave retail, historic Central Memorial Park, and public art.
entities.description: Positioned immediately south of the Canadian Pacific mainline and downtown towers, the Beltline is Calgary’s most dense and bustling urban neighborhood. Renowned for 17th Avenue SW (the Red Mile), the annual BUMP festival mural galleries, and Central Memorial Park.

sources.name: Beltline Urban Development & City of Calgary

image.alt: Beltline 17th Avenue SW and Central Memorial Park

entities.title: Bridgeland-Riverside
entities.summary: A sun-drenched escarpment village known for Italian bakeries, Murdock Park panoramic skyline views, and riverside parklets.
entities.description: Nestled between the bluff hills and the north bank of the Bow River, Bridgeland is renowned for its welcoming European café culture along 1st Avenue NE, the scenic 4th Street flyover connection to downtown, and extensive community programming centered at the BRCA hall.

image.alt: Bridgeland 1st Avenue NE and skyline views from Murdoch Park

entities.title: Marda Loop
entities.summary: Southwest Calgary’s favourite creative high street, featuring 33rd Avenue boutiques, cSPACE Marda Loop arts incubator, and lively patios.
entities.description: Taking its name from the historic Marda Theatre and the streetcar turnaround loop, Marda Loop has grown into a bustling pedestrian destination anchored along 33rd and 34th Avenues SW. Cultural life converges at cSPACE King Edward, a heritage sandstone school transformed into studios and weekend farmers markets.

image.alt: Marda Loop 33rd Avenue pedestrian streetscape

entities.title: Bowness
entities.summary: A storied Bow Valley river town incorporated into Calgary, celebrated for Bowness Park lagoon, mature cottonwood groves, and small-town spirit.
entities.description: Once an independent town destination connected by streetcar, Bowness maintains an unmistakable pride of place along the Bow River. Home to Bowness Park’s iconic boat lagoon and winter ice trail, Main Street (Bowness Road) local shops, and direct access to Shouldice Park.

sources.name: Bowness Community Association & City of Calgary

image.alt: Bowness Park lagoon and pathway bridge

entities.title: Ramsay
entities.summary: Hilltop heritage community overlooking the confluence, featuring red-brick alleyways, artisan workshops, and sweeping Stampede Park vistas.
entities.description: Directly east of the Elbow River and south of Inglewood, Ramsay climbs the Scotsman’s Hill escarpment. Renowned for its preserved historic workers’ cottages, active laneway tool shares, independent design studios, and the iconic city panorama from Scotsman’s Hill.

image.alt: Ramsay historic cottage streetscape and skyline ridge

entries.note: Coffee in Kensington, a five-minute walk from the Peace Bridge.

entities.title: A Day Along the Bow
entities.summary: Inglewood to the Peace Bridge on the river pathway: whitewater, an island park, the Central Library and a free skyline view to finish.
entities.description: A flat, paved, free walk west along the Bow River pathway, from the rapids at Harvie Passage to the Peace Bridge, with the confluence, St. Patrick’s Island, the Central Library and Prince’s Island Park on the way. Finish with the climb to the Crescent Heights lookout for the view most postcards use.

sources.name: City of Calgary: pathways and bikeways

image.alt: The Peace Bridge over the Bow River

entities.introduction: The Bow is the reason Calgary is where it is, and the pathway along it is the best free thing in the city. This route walks it east to west, so the downtown skyline grows in front of you all afternoon.
entities.methodology: Walked and timed by CalgaryWatch. Every stop is on or within a few minutes of the paved river pathway, free to visit, and has washrooms or a café close by. Nobody paid to be on this list.

facts.season: Year round. Main pathways are plowed in winter.

stops.name: Pearce Estate Park and Harvie Passage
stops.mapQuery: Pearce Estate Park, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Start where the river is loudest. Harvie Passage replaced the old Calgary weir, long nicknamed the drowning machine, with rapids that paddlers and rafters can run and a channel that lets fish through.
stops.tip: Watch from the bank. The rapids are for experienced paddlers only.

stops.name: Fort Calgary and the confluence
stops.mapQuery: Fort Calgary, 750 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: The Elbow meets the Bow here, and in 1875 the North-West Mounted Police built the fort the city grew out of. The grounds and the river edge are free to wander.

stops.name: St. Patrick’s Island
stops.mapQuery: St. Patrick’s Island Park, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A whole island park a bridge away from downtown, with a pebble beach, a sledding hill and Bloom, a tall sculpture built from retired city streetlights.
stops.tip: Cross on the George C. King Bridge, the one shaped like a skipping stone.

stops.name: Central Library
stops.mapQuery: Calgary Central Library, 800 3 St SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Five minutes off the river and worth the detour. The wooden arch of the entrance frames the CTrain running underneath, and it is free, warm and has the best public washrooms downtown.

stops.name: Prince’s Island Park
stops.mapQuery: Prince’s Island Park, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Downtown’s back garden: lawns, lagoons and the River Café in the middle. In July it fills up for the Calgary Folk Music Festival.
stops.tip: The lagoon side is the quiet side.

stops.name: Peace Bridge
stops.mapQuery: Peace Bridge, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Santiago Calatrava’s red helix, open since 2012 and only for people on foot or on bikes. Cross it slowly; everyone stops for a photo halfway.

stops.name: Crescent Heights lookout
stops.mapQuery: Crescent Road NW lookout, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Climb the McHugh Bluff stairs from Sunnyside to Crescent Road for the classic view back over the river and the whole skyline. Best at sunset.
stops.tip: Sunnyside CTrain station is a short walk back down when you are done.

tips: Bikes and scooters share the pathway. Keep right and say “on your left” when you pass.
In June the river runs high and fast. Stay off the banks and out of the water.
Going one way? Sunnyside station on the Red Line gets you home from the finish.

entities.title: Calgary’s Farmers’ Markets, Big and Small
entities.summary: The two big indoor halls for any week of the year, the old-school weekend market, and the community markets worth planning a Saturday around.
entities.description: Calgary’s markets come in three sizes: the year-round indoor halls, Crossroads with its flea-market corner, and the neighbourhood markets run by community associations. This guide covers each one, what it is good for, and links to the next confirmed date we have for it.

image.alt: Friends making plans together in the city

entities.introduction: Every part of the city has its own market ritual. The big halls will feed you any week of the year; the small community markets are where you meet the grower and end up chatting for ten minutes.
entities.methodology: Every market here is one CalgaryWatch already tracks, with dates checked against the organizer. Each stop links to its listing, so the next date you see is the one we last confirmed, not a guess. Nobody paid to be on this list.

facts.season: Halls year round. Community markets mostly June to October.

stops.name: Calgary Farmers’ Market South
stops.mapQuery: Calgary Farmers’ Market South, 510 77 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: The big one. A huge indoor hall of butchers, bakers, produce stalls and lunch counters, open Thursday to Sunday all year.
stops.tip: Go before 11 on Saturdays, or go Thursday and have it to yourself.

stops.name: Calgary Farmers’ Market West
stops.mapQuery: Calgary Farmers’ Market West, 25 Greenbriar Dr NW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: The same idea in a newer, brighter building on the west side. Easy stop on the way out to the mountains.

stops.name: Crossroads Market
stops.mapQuery: Crossroads Market, 1235 26 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Old-school and a bit chaotic, in the best way. Produce and food stalls on one side, antiques and flea-market finds on the other.
stops.tip: Bring cash for the flea-market side.

stops.name: Hillhurst Sunnyside Farmers’ Market
stops.mapQuery: Hillhurst Sunnyside Community Association, 1320 5 Ave NW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A summer community market run by the neighbourhood, a short walk from Kensington. Small, friendly and very local.

stops.name: Bridgeland-Riverside Farmers’ Market
stops.mapQuery: Bridgeland-Riverside Community Association, 917 Centre Ave NE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A community-hall market on the hill above the river. Pair it with a walk down to the Bow.

stops.name: Farmers & Makers Market at cSPACE
stops.mapQuery: cSPACE King Edward, 1721 29 Ave SW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Growers and makers inside a restored sandstone school that is now an arts hub. Come for the market, stay for the building.

stops.name: Dalhousie Harvest Farmers’ Market
stops.mapQuery: 5432 Dalhart Rd NW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A northwest community market with growers you will not find downtown.

stops.name: Calgary Winter Market
stops.mapQuery: 101 Barclay Parade SW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: When the summer markets pack up, this one keeps a downtown market going through the cold months.

tips: Bakeries sell out first. If bread is the point, go early.
Bring a tote and some cash. Smaller stalls at community markets do not always take cards.
Seasonal markets mostly run June to October. The two big halls carry you through winter.

entities.title: Inglewood & Ramsay on Foot
entities.summary: Calgary’s oldest main street, a record store that has outlasted everything, a bird sanctuary, a warehouse brewery and the best free view of downtown.
entities.description: A day on foot in Inglewood and Ramsay, east of downtown. Start at the fort the city grew from, work along 9 Avenue SE for records and coffee, slip out to the bird sanctuary, and finish on Scotsman’s Hill at sunset with live blues after.

sources.name: City of Calgary: Inglewood Bird Sanctuary

image.alt: The Calgary Tower above downtown at golden hour

entities.introduction: Inglewood calls itself Calgary’s oldest neighbourhood, and 9 Avenue SE still looks the part: low brick storefronts, independent shops and almost no chains. Ramsay sits on the hill next door and has the view.
entities.methodology: Walked by CalgaryWatch. Every stop is independent, local, and open to anyone; the brewery and the bar are 18+ in the evening. Independent places change hours often, so check before you go. Nobody paid to be on this list.

facts.season: Best spring to fall. The sanctuary is open year round.

stops.name: Fort Calgary
stops.mapQuery: Fort Calgary, 750 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Where it started: the 1875 police fort at the confluence. Walk the grounds and the river edge, then head east on 9 Avenue.

stops.name: Recordland
stops.mapQuery: Recordland, 1208 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Floor-to-ceiling crates of vinyl that have been here for decades. Bring time, not a plan.

stops.name: Rosso Coffee Roasters
stops.mapQuery: Rosso Coffee Roasters, 1402 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A Calgary roaster on the main street. Take it to go and keep walking.

stops.name: Inglewood Bird Sanctuary
stops.mapQuery: Inglewood Bird Sanctuary, 2425 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A quiet, flat loop through riverside forest where hundreds of bird species have been spotted. Free, and the calmest hour you will spend in the city.
stops.tip: No dogs or bikes inside. Mornings are best for birds.

stops.name: Cold Garden Beverage Company
stops.mapQuery: Cold Garden Beverage Company, 1100 11 St SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A big, cheerful warehouse taproom. Grab a table, a pint and a second wind.

stops.name: Scotsman’s Hill
stops.mapQuery: Scotsman’s Hill, Salisbury St SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: The best free view of downtown, with the Stampede grounds right below you. Come for sunset; during Stampede week people bring chairs for the fireworks.

stops.name: The Blues Can
stops.mapQuery: The Blues Can, 1429 9 Ave SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Finish where Inglewood has finished its nights for years: a small room with live blues on stage.
stops.tip: 18+. Check the lineup and any cover charge before you go.

tips: Parking on 9 Avenue fills up on weekends. The 1 bus and the walk from downtown are easier.
Most shops open around 10 or 11; plan the sanctuary for the morning.
Scotsman’s Hill is a residential street. Keep it quiet for the neighbours.

entities.title: Calgary for $0
entities.summary: A whole downtown day that costs nothing, built to work in January: a glass garden, 16 km of skywalks, the city’s best library and a skyline view at the end.
entities.description: A free day in downtown Calgary that works in any weather. Go indoors through the +15 skywalks and Devonian Gardens, out along Stephen Avenue and through Chinatown, and finish on the river and up at the Crescent Heights lookout.

image.alt: Downtown Calgary skyline

entities.introduction: Calgary is expensive enough. This is a full day downtown without paying for a ticket, a museum or parking, and most of it is indoors, so it works at minus twenty as well as in July.
entities.methodology: Picked by CalgaryWatch. Every stop is free to enter, open to the public and reachable on foot or by CTrain. We list what something costs only when it is truly zero. Nobody paid to be on this list.

stops.name: Central Library
stops.mapQuery: Calgary Central Library, 800 3 St SE, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Start somewhere warm and beautiful. Wander all the floors, find a window seat, and if you live here, get a library card: it is free.
stops.tip: The kids’ floor is one of the best free play spaces in the city.

stops.name: Stephen Avenue Walk
stops.mapQuery: Stephen Avenue Walk, 8 Ave SW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Calgary’s pedestrian main street, lined with sandstone buildings from the early 1900s. Walk it west and look up.

stops.name: Devonian Gardens
stops.mapQuery: Devonian Gardens, 317 7 Ave SW, Calgary, AB
stops.note: A free indoor garden under a glass roof, with thousands of plants, a koi pond and a living wall. The warmest green space in the city in February.

stops.name: The +15 skywalks
stops.mapQuery: Plus 15 skywalk, downtown Calgary, AB
stops.note: About 16 km of enclosed bridges, one floor up, linking a big part of downtown. Follow the +15 signs and cross the core without stepping outside.
stops.tip: Some bridges close in the evening and on weekends. Weekdays are best.

stops.name: Chinatown and Sien Lok Park
stops.mapQuery: Sien Lok Park, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Walk Centre Street into Chinatown, then down to Sien Lok Park on the river. Budget a few dollars if a bakery gets you; that part is optional.

stops.name: Prince’s Island Park and the Peace Bridge
stops.mapQuery: Prince’s Island Park, Calgary, AB
stops.note: Back outside for the river: loop the island, then cross Santiago Calatrava’s red Peace Bridge to Sunnyside.

stops.name: Crescent Heights lookout
stops.mapQuery: Crescent Road NW lookout, Calgary, AB
stops.note: End with the climb up the McHugh Bluff stairs to Crescent Road for the whole skyline at sunset. Still free.

tips: CTrain rides in the downtown free fare zone along 7 Avenue cost nothing. Check Calgary Transit for the current zone.
Kids 12 and under ride Calgary Transit free.
Bring a water bottle. The library and the gardens have fountains.

entities.name: Calgary Chinese Cultural Centre
entities.title: Calgary Chinese Cultural Centre
entities.summary: A Chinatown cultural hub for Chinese arts, language, wellness, recreation and community celebrations throughout the year.
entities.description: The Calgary Chinese Cultural Centre is a charitable non-profit gathering place serving Chinatown, Calgary’s Chinese community and Calgarians more broadly. Its year-round programs span Chinese arts and heritage, Mandarin, calligraphy and painting, music and dance, Tai Chi and Qigong, martial arts, recreation, wellness, and family and senior activities. Current fall 2026 sessions include Wing Chun, Adult Mandarin, Chinese Xie Yi Painting, Table Tennis and beginner Yang Style Tai Chi. Dates and registration can change, so use the Centre’s official programs and events pages for the current schedule.

images.alt: Illustrated Calgary festival scene with live music, food, cyclists and people gathering beside the river

entities.name: Rosso Coffee Roasters — Inglewood
entities.title: Rosso Coffee Roasters — Inglewood
entities.summary: Direct-trade coffee roasted right in SE Calgary, served alongside fresh sourdough pastries in a light-filled industrial brick room.
entities.description: A beloved Calgary institution since 2007. Rosso’s Inglewood outpost offers single-origin pour-overs, cold brew, and a welcoming meeting space for neighbours and Bow River cyclists.

image.alt: Rosso Coffee Roasters café patio on 9th Ave SE

images.alt: Rosso Coffee Roasters interior and espresso machine

entities.name: Higher Ground Café — Kensington
entities.title: Higher Ground Café — Kensington
entities.summary: A staple 10th Street NW gathering place serving 100% organic, fair-trade coffee and warm comfort meals until late.
entities.description: An anchor of Kensington for over twenty years. Features a fireplace, local art displays on brick walls, and late operating hours popular with university students and neighbours.

image.alt: Higher Ground Cafe on 10th Street NW Kensington

entities.name: cSPACE Marda Loop Creative Hub
entities.title: cSPACE Marda Loop Creative Hub
entities.summary: A historic sandstone school turned vibrant multi-disciplinary creative hub with galleries, studios, and weekend farmers markets.
entities.description: Preserving the historic 1912 King Edward School, cSPACE provides workspace for more than 30 artists, creative entrepreneurs, a community coffee shop, and regular indoor-outdoor artisan fairs.

image.alt: cSPACE Marda Loop sandstone schoolhouse and courtyard

entities.name: Luke’s Drug Mart — Bridgeland
entities.title: Luke’s Drug Mart — Bridgeland
entities.summary: Calgary’s oldest independent pharmacy, transformed into a cultural hub with specialty vinyl, soft serve ice cream, and espresso.
entities.description: Operating in Bridgeland since 1951, Luke’s blends a neighborhood pharmacy with curated vinyl records, specialty groceries, Four Barrel espresso, and seasonal soft serve.

sources.name: Luke’s Drug Mart Official & Bridgeland BRZ

image.alt: Luke’s Drug Mart in Bridgeland

images.alt: Luke’s Drug Mart shelves and vinyl records

entities.name: Vertigo Theatre
entities.title: Vertigo Theatre
entities.summary: A downtown Calgary theatre devoted to mystery, suspense and stories that keep audiences guessing.
entities.description: Vertigo Theatre presents a full season of professional live theatre in Calgary Tower Centre, with a long-running focus on mystery, thriller and suspense. Its 50th-anniversary 2026–27 season includes six productions, from the world premiere of The Lodger to Sherlock Holmes, The 39 Steps and a new Detective Murdoch mystery. Check Vertigo’s official season page for current performance times and tickets.

images.alt: Illustrated Calgary festival scene with performers and people gathering beside the river

entities.name: Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo
entities.title: Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo
entities.summary: Calgary’s zoo by the Bow River, run by the Wilder Institute conservation charity, with animals from around the world and seasonal events all year.
entities.description: Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo is home to animals from around the world, gardens and a year-round calendar of seasonal events, from ZooBOO at Halloween to Sunday Safari Brunch. The zoo is run by the Wilder Institute, a conservation charity. Hours, tickets and event details change through the year, so the zoo’s official website is the source of truth for anything you plan around.
entities.address: 1300 Zoo Road NE, Calgary, AB T2E 7V6

images.alt: Illustrated Calgary festival scene with performers and people gathering beside the river

entities.name: Downstage
entities.title: Downstage
entities.summary: A Calgary theatre company making socially engaged new work, performing at the Motel Theatre in the Werklund Centre.
entities.description: Downstage creates and presents new Calgary theatre about the issues people are living with now, and builds conversation around each show. Its 2026–27 season at the Motel Theatre in the Werklund Centre includes Dreaming Climate Consciousness (October 23 and 24, four short plays set in one shared climate future), Creative Stretch on Mondays from October to May, and A Study of Choices (April 7 to 11, 2027). More dates are added through the year, so check Downstage’s current season page for times and tickets.
entities.address: Motel Theatre, Werklund Centre, 205 8 Avenue SE, Calgary, AB

image.alt: Downstage 2026–2027 season poster featuring artwork for From Scratch, Dreaming Climate Consciousness, A Study of Choices and Creative Stretch

images.alt: Downstage 2026–2027 season poster featuring artwork for From Scratch, Dreaming Climate Consciousness, A Study of Choices and Creative Stretch

entities.name: Ghost River Theatre
entities.title: Ghost River Theatre
entities.summary: A Calgary devised-theatre company making original, often immersive work, based at the West Village Theatre in Sunalta.
entities.description: Ghost River Theatre creates original devised theatre, built by its artists from the ground up and often immersive. It doesn’t run a fixed subscription season: projects are developed, staged and toured over time, and its 2026/27 Experiences page lists what is in the works. Ghost River’s main website carries the most current dates, so check it before you plan a night out.
entities.address: West Village Theatre, 2007 10 Avenue SW, Calgary, AB

entities.title: Theatre Calgary
entities.name: Theatre Calgary
entities.summary: Calgary theatre company presenting performances at the Max Bell Theatre.
entities.description: Find Theatre Calgary performances and follow its official website for the current season, tickets and production details. CalgaryWatch links associated performances below; individual dates and availability remain with the company.

entities.title: Alliance Française de Calgary
entities.name: Alliance Française de Calgary
entities.summary: Discover Alliance Française de Calgary through its official homepage.
entities.description: Use the organization’s homepage for its current activities and published information. CalgaryWatch links officially sourced associated events here when available. Check the official site for locations, schedules and registration.

entities.title: Werklund Centre
entities.name: Werklund Centre
entities.summary: Downtown Calgary performing arts centre, formerly Arts Commons.
entities.description: Werklund Centre is a home for performing arts in downtown Calgary. Visit its official website for current programming and visitor information. Events held in its venues are not automatically events organized by the centre; only officially attributed organizer events appear below.

entities.title: Inglewood Business Improvement Area
entities.name: Inglewood Business Improvement Area
entities.summary: The business improvement area organizing events and supporting local businesses in Inglewood.
entities.description: The business improvement area organizing events and supporting local businesses in Inglewood. Confirm upcoming dates with the organization’s official website.

entities.title: Dalhousie Community Association
entities.name: Dalhousie Community Association
entities.summary: The community association behind the Dalhousie Harvest Farmers’ Market.
entities.description: The community association behind the Dalhousie Harvest Farmers’ Market. Confirm upcoming dates with the organization’s official website.

entities.title: Alberta Theatre Projects
entities.name: Alberta Theatre Projects
entities.summary: Alberta Theatre Projects presents theatre at the Martha Cohen Theatre in Calgary.
entities.description: Visit Alberta Theatre Projects’ official website for its current season, performance information and organization details. Its own productions appear below; events presented by other organizations at the same venue are not attributed to ATP.

entities.title: Heritage Park Historical Village
entities.name: Heritage Park Historical Village
entities.summary: A Calgary heritage attraction with ghost tours, seasonal activities and special events.
entities.description: Explore Heritage Park’s own programme of tours and seasonal events. Check the individual event page for admission, entry times and which areas are open.

entities.title: The Confluence Historic Site & Parkland
entities.name: The Confluence Historic Site & Parkland
entities.summary: A Calgary gathering place for history, talks, creative workshops and cultural events.
entities.description: The Confluence’s programme includes talks, film nights, crafts and community gatherings. Find the events it organizes below and check its official pages for current registration and visitor information.

entities.title: Contemporary Calgary
entities.name: Contemporary Calgary
entities.summary: Contemporary art exhibitions, artist talks and creative programmes in Calgary.
entities.description: Discover exhibitions and public programmes at Contemporary Calgary. Exhibition runs and separately scheduled talks or workshops may have different admission and registration requirements; use each official event page before visiting.

entities.title: Calgary Opera
entities.name: Calgary Opera
entities.summary: Calgary opera productions and special performances.
entities.description: Calgary Opera presents staged productions and special performances. Locations vary by event; the Southern Alberta Jubilee Auditorium is a performance venue rather than an office address for this profile. Check the official production page for language, surtitles, dates and tickets.

entities.title: Wordfest
entities.name: Wordfest
entities.summary: Author conversations and literary performances, including the Imaginairium festival.
entities.description: Wordfest brings writers and readers together through author conversations, literary performances and its Imaginairium festival. Events use several Calgary venues; check each listing for the actual location, admission and accessibility details.

entities.title: Alberta Ballet
entities.name: Alberta Ballet
entities.summary: Ballet performances in Calgary, including The Nutcracker.
entities.description: Find Alberta Ballet’s Calgary performances and follow its official production pages for current dates and tickets. Performance venues are listed on the individual events; this organization profile does not present the Jubilee Auditorium as the company’s office.

entities.title: Calgary Farmers' Market
entities.name: Calgary Farmers' Market
entities.summary: One market organization with South and West Calgary locations.
entities.description: Explore the South and West market locations below. Each location keeps its own address and scheduled market days; check the location’s official page for current hours and holiday exceptions.

entities.title: Calgary Earth Market Society
entities.name: Calgary Earth Market Society
entities.summary: Organizer of the Farmers & Makers Market at cSPACE.
entities.description: Find the Farmers & Makers Market at cSPACE below, with its own location and scheduled market days. The market is organized by Calgary Earth Market Society; cSPACE is the host location. Check the organizer’s page for seasonal changes.

entities.title: Crossroads Market
entities.name: Crossroads Market
entities.summary: A year-round Calgary market for fresh food, independent vendors, local shopping and a food hall.
entities.description: Operating since 1987, Crossroads brings together fresh food, groceries, specialty vendors, restaurants and independent makers. The regular market opens Friday–Sunday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m., with free parking. Vendor applications are available through the organization. Guest markets at this location may have different organizers and hours.

entities.title: Hillhurst Sunnyside Community Association
entities.name: Hillhurst Sunnyside Community Association
entities.summary: The community organization behind Hillhurst Sunnyside Farmers’ Market.
entities.description: The HSCA farmers’ market connects neighbours with local food producers, artisans and makers. The year-round Wednesday market runs 3–7 p.m. The indoor season runs October 14, 2026–May 12, 2027. Sunnyside CTrain is about a five-minute walk away; check the market site for seasonal arrangements.

sources.name: Hillhurst Sunnyside Community Association — supplied source research

entities.title: Little Modern Market
entities.name: Little Modern Market
entities.summary: A Calgary pop-up market connecting local makers, artists, boutiques and small businesses.
entities.description: Established in 2016, Little Modern Market brings local makers, artists, boutiques and food vendors together with a community charity component, typically featuring 100–120 vendors per market. Its 2026 venue is the Red & White Club / Olympic Volunteer Centre at McMahon Stadium, 1833 Crowchild Trail NW. Admission is free with an encouraged donation to the featured charity. Certified service dogs only; check each edition for activities and workshops.

sources.name: Holiday market hours corroboration supplied by user

entities.title: Fresh & Local Market + Kitchens
entities.name: Fresh & Local Market + Kitchens
entities.address: #426, 12445 Lake Fraser Drive SE, Calgary, AB T2J 7A4
entities.summary: A year-round indoor local-food market and culinary marketplace in Avenida Village.
entities.description: Fresh & Local combines regional food producers, prepared food, culinary kitchens and specialty vendors. The organization describes more than 275 local producers and around 40 culinary kitchens and food artisans. Its 2026 food-festival programme included monthly celebrations through September. Follow the official news and events page for new programming.

entities.title: MAKERS
entities.name: MAKERS
entities.summary: Canadian maker marketplaces at Market Mall, The CORE and Southcentre.
entities.description: MAKERS showcases independent Canadian makers through permanent retail marketplaces featuring jewellery, art, candles, apparel, home décor and gifts. Calgary locations at Market Mall, The CORE and Southcentre keep their own hours and contact emails. These are permanent retail locations, not separately announced craft fairs. CrossIron Mills is outside this Calgary-only set.

entities.title: The Barn Artisan Market
entities.name: The Barn Artisan Market
entities.address: Shawnessy Barn, 224 Shawmeadows Road SW, Calgary, AB
entities.summary: An artisan market at Shawnessy Barn with Alberta-made goods and a changing local vendor lineup.
entities.description: Established in January 2020, The Barn Artisan Market features more than 30 local vendors across two floors of Shawnessy Barn. Admission and parking are free. Products must be handcrafted, created or made in Alberta; MLM, direct sales and drop-shipping are excluded. The usual fourth-Sunday pattern has exceptions: the 2026 Christmas Market is November 29. Check the calendar below for confirmed market dates.

sources.name: The Barn Artisan Market — supplied source research

entities.title: Calgary Yuletide Festival Society
entities.name: Calgary Yuletide Festival Society
entities.summary: The nonprofit organizer behind Calgary Winter Market at Eau Claire Plaza.
entities.description: Calgary Yuletide Festival Society organizes Calgary Winter Market, a European-inspired outdoor holiday market with retail huts, food and drinks, entertainment, children’s activities, a carousel and a Brauhaus tent. The 2026 edition runs on selected days November 19–December 24 at Eau Claire Plaza. The market location is listed separately from the organization’s base.

entities.title: YMCA Calgary
entities.name: YMCA Calgary

entities.summary: A Calgary nonprofit operating recreation centres, camps, child development and community programming.
entities.description: YMCA Calgary connects communities through recreation, camps, child development and community programmes. Its free 2026 Winter Markets bring local vendors to four branches across five dates. The Kensington address is the association office; each winter-market listing has its own branch location and contact email.

sources.name: YMCA Calgary contacts (media email; branch contacts preferred for markets)

entities.title: Signatures Shows
entities.name: Signatures Shows
entities.summary: Canadian handmade-market producer behind Calgary’s Festival of Crafts.
entities.description: Family-owned since 1980, Signatures brings together independent Canadian artists, artisans, makers and designers. Its Calgary show, Festival of Crafts, runs October 29–November 1, 2026 at the BMO Centre, Hall F. The event venue is separate from the organizer’s base. Calgary show inquiries can go to show manager Samantha Milner at smilner@signatures.ca.

entities.title: Millarville Racing and Agricultural Society
entities.name: Millarville Racing and Agricultural Society
entities.summary: A Foothills agricultural society hosting markets, fairs and community gatherings.
entities.description: A nearby day trip outside Calgary, the society hosts seasonal farmers’ markets, the Priddis & Millarville Fair, horse racing and community gatherings. Its 2026 Christmas Market runs November 5–8 and November 12–15. The summer market finished October 10; no unannounced future summer dates are listed.

entities.title: The Saskatoon Farm
entities.name: The Saskatoon Farm
entities.address: #20, 80181 338 Avenue East, Foothills County, AB T1S 4S3
entities.summary: A family-run Foothills farm with seasonal produce, a bakery, restaurant and greenhouse gatherings.
entities.description: Family-run since 1987, The Saskatoon Farm combines seasonal farm shopping, a bakery, restaurant and garden centre with workshops and celebrations. This is a day trip outside Calgary. Its upcoming official calendar includes an October 23 felted-art workshop and October 30 Día de los Muertos celebration. Check the farm’s seasonal updates before travelling; farmers’ market hours and winter closure are separate from event hours.

entities.title: Granary Road
entities.name: Granary Road
entities.address: 226066 112 Street West, Foothills County, AB T1S 5S5
entities.summary: A Foothills family destination with farm experiences, indoor exhibits and a Christmas market.
entities.description: A day trip south of Calgary, Granary Road’s 2026 Christmas Market runs on three weekends, November 28–29, December 5–6 and December 12–13, 10 a.m.–4 p.m. Market admission is required; selected Christmas activity passes include entry. The outdoor park and mini golf reopen in spring 2027, while the Fabulous & Fantastic Farm indoor exhibit opens weekends. Do not confuse indoor-exhibit admission with market admission.

entities.title: Bowness Community Association
entities.name: Bowness Community Association
entities.summary: A neighbourhood association with community programming, recreation and a local-maker holiday fair.
entities.description: Established in 1963, the BCA offers community events, programming and facility rentals. Its free Holiday Craft Fair brings handmade goods and local makers to the Main Hall on November 14–15, 2026, 10 a.m.–4 p.m. The official fair contact is craftfair@mybowness.com; vendor applications have closed.

entities.title: Triwood Community Association
entities.name: Triwood Community Association
entities.address: 2244 Chicoutimi Drive NW, Calgary, AB T2L 0W1
entities.summary: A northwest community association with seasonal markets, recreation and neighbourhood events.
entities.description: Triwood offers community markets, fitness, social clubs, an arena, camps and facility rentals. Its free Halloween Skate Night takes place October 25, 2026. Check the organizer’s market calendar for seasonal editions and current details.

entities.title: Acadia Community Association
entities.name: Acadia Community Association
entities.summary: A southeast community association hosting a free Christmas market and neighbourhood programming.
entities.description: The ACA supports neighbours through social and recreational programming, community advocacy and events. Its 2026 Christmas Market takes place November 14, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., in Rose Hall at the Acadia Recreation Complex. Admission and parking are free. Market questions: events@acadiaca.com.

entities.title: Silver Springs Community Association
entities.name: Silver Springs Community Association
entities.address: 5720 Silver Ridge Drive NW, Calgary, AB T3B 5E5
entities.summary: A northwest nonprofit with community programmes and a free local-artisan Christmas market.
entities.description: Serving Silver Springs since 1975, the association offers programmes, rental spaces and events for neighbours of all ages. Its Christmas Craft Market runs November 14, 2026, 10 a.m.–3 p.m., with handmade goods, unique gifts and local crafts. The market is free to attend and open to all.

entities.title: Deerfoot City
entities.name: Deerfoot City
entities.summary: An open-air shopping destination with seasonal family events along The Boulevard.
entities.description: Deerfoot City combines shopping, dining and entertainment with family-friendly seasonal programming. Destination: Boo City includes trick-or-treating and hands-on science on October 24, 2026, 6–8 p.m. Its pumpkin patch has separate hours and a food-bank donation requirement; confirm that schedule directly. Event and media inquiries are handled by the marketing team at gs@deerfootcity.ca.

entities.title: ScreamFest
entities.name: ScreamFest
entities.summary: A Calgary Halloween attraction with haunted houses, scare zones and midway rides.
entities.description: ScreamFest brings haunted attractions to GMC Stadium, Stampede Park on select October nights. Expect haunted houses, scare zones and midway rides; much of the experience is outdoors. Check the official site for tickets, age restrictions and the adults-only night. The show venue is listed on individual events, separate from this organizer profile.

entities.title: The Mercantile on 9th
entities.name: The Mercantile on 9th
entities.summary: Inglewood's sustainability-minded seasonal artisan market, presented by The Apothecary in Inglewood.
entities.description: The Mercantile brings local makers, growers, artists and bakers together at the Alexandra Centre in Inglewood. The Apothecary in Inglewood created and presents the market.

entities.title: Calgary Philharmonic Orchestra
entities.name: Calgary Philharmonic Orchestra
entities.summary: Calgary’s orchestra, with a full season of concerts at the Jack Singer Concert Hall.
entities.description: The Calgary Philharmonic Orchestra presents its 2026/27 season mostly at the Jack Singer Concert Hall at Werklund Centre, with some concerts at other venues such as Mount Royal University’s Bella Concert Hall. Locations vary by concert; check the official concert page for the programme, times and tickets. Cpossibilities members aged 13 to 35 can buy discounted tickets to select concerts, and seniors and students can attend some open rehearsals.

entities.title: Inside Out Theatre
entities.name: Inside Out Theatre
entities.summary: A Calgary disability theatre company, and the team behind the Good Host accessible performances.
entities.description: Inside Out Theatre is a disability theatre company in Calgary, equally invested in artistic excellence, community development and deepening our culture’s accessibility. Through its Good Host Program it works with other Calgary theatres on accessible performances of their shows. Its full list of events is on its official events page, which is the source CalgaryWatch uses for dates.

entities.title: Spiritus Chamber Choir
entities.name: Spiritus Chamber Choir
entities.summary: A Calgary chamber choir in its 30th season.
entities.description: Spiritus Chamber Choir is a Calgary chamber choir. Its 2026–2027 season, the choir’s 30th, runs across four concerts and opens with The Turning Season on November 8. Venues vary by concert; check the choir’s tickets page for dates, venues and prices.

entities.title: Morpheus Theatre
entities.name: Morpheus Theatre
entities.summary: Calgary community theatre staging comedies, mysteries and Gilbert and Sullivan at the Pumphouse Theatre.
entities.description: Morpheus Theatre is in its 32nd season of what it calls Shows Worth Seeing, with productions at the Pumphouse Theatre and a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera to close each season. Its own website is kept current, so check its season page for show dates, times and tickets.

entities.title: Pumphouse Theatres
entities.name: Pumphouse Theatres
entities.address: 2140 Pumphouse Avenue SW, Calgary, AB T3C 3P5
entities.summary: Two theatres in Calgary's historic water pumphouse beside the Bow River, home to independent and community productions.
entities.description: Pumphouse Theatres runs two performance spaces in a converted 1913 pumping station near the Bow River in Sunalta. Independent and community companies rent the stages for plays, musicals and festivals through the year, so the line-up changes show by show. Check the Pumphouse's own website for what's on and how to get tickets.

entities.title: Calgary Underground Film Festival
entities.name: Calgary Underground Film Festival
entities.summary: Calgary's festival of cult, genre, documentary and offbeat independent film, held each spring.
entities.description: The Calgary Underground Film Festival (CUFF) screens independent features, shorts and documentaries that sit outside the mainstream, from horror and comedy to music films. The main festival runs each spring, with special screenings through the year. Dates, programme and passes are announced on CUFF's own website.

sources.name: Calgary Underground Film Festival — official website

entities.title: Calgary Queer Arts Society
entities.name: Calgary Queer Arts Society
entities.summary: The society behind Fairy Tales Queer Art & Film Festival, Calgary's long-running 2SLGBTQIA+ film festival.
entities.description: The Calgary Queer Arts Society (formerly the Fairy Tales Presentation Society) presents Fairy Tales Queer Art & Film Festival each spring, with feature films, shorts, art and community events by and about 2SLGBTQIA+ people. The 2026 festival ran May 13 to 17 at Contemporary Calgary. Future dates are announced on the society's own website.

entities.name: Calaway Park

entities.description: Calaway Park is a seasonal amusement park with rides, games, live entertainment and a campground on the western edge of Calgary. It opens in late spring and runs through the summer, with fall weekend events. Season dates, hours and passes are on the park's own website.

entities.title: Brentwood Community Association
entities.name: Brentwood Community Association

entities.description: The Brentwood Community Association runs programs, events and its community hall for neighbours in Brentwood, and hosts a Christmas craft market each November. Dates, programs and hall bookings are on the association's own website.

entities.name: Leighton Art Centre

It runs exhibitions, art classes, school programs and summer camps, and admission is by donation. Hours and programs are on the centre's own website.

entities.title: Calgary Youth Orchestra
entities.name: Calgary Youth Orchestra

entities.summary: Calgary's youth symphony orchestra, giving young musicians a full concert season.
entities.description: The Calgary Youth Orchestra gives young musicians orchestral training and a season of public concerts. It is based at Mount Royal University's Conservatory. Concert dates and audition information are on the orchestra's own website.

entities.title: Village Brewery

entities.title: Taste of Calgary
entities.name: Taste of Calgary

entities.description: Taste of Calgary is an outdoor food festival held each summer, where local restaurants and food vendors serve sample-size dishes alongside drinks and live entertainment. entities.title: Stage West Theatre Restaurant
entities.name: Stage West Theatre Restaurant
